title: Usage Tally Accordion — Cost attribution, export flows & pricing pattern playbook
creator: Amira Patel
description:
Summary: A design playbook and prototype for a collapsible 'Usage Tally' accordion component inside the Redwood Console that surfaces token-level cost breakdowns, attribution links, and exportable slices. The goal is a compact default dashboard row that expands to show multi-dimensional cost attribution (route, model variant, prompt template, time slice) and a lightweight export flow for CSV/BigQuery streaming.

Goals:
- Reduce cognitive load: show a single-line summary with clear P50/P95 token cost and burst delta, expandable into detailed attribution.
- Make exports first-class: one-click CSV and schema-backed BigQuery export with field-level explanations.
- Enable pricing patterns: expose quick toggles for slab vs tiered vs negotiated pricing previews in-context.
- Support rollouts: component must support canary states and fallbacks for dedicated/private deployments.

User stories:
- As an engineering lead, I want to quickly see which route generated the highest token spend in the last 24h, and export that slice for chargeback.
- As a finance analyst, I want to preview how a tiered pricing slab would change bill estimates for a selected time range.
- As a PM, I want to attach the expanded attribution view to a ticket with a permalink and include the exact export schema.

Acceptance criteria:
- Collapsed row shows: route name, total tokens, token cost estimate, 24h delta, and a three-dot menu with 'Export' and 'Open Attribution'.
- Expanded view shows: stacked attribution bars (model, prompt-template, user-segmentation), top contributors list (top 5), and export controls including custom time-slicing and pricing preview.
- Export options: CSV download and 'Stream to BigQuery' with selectable project/dataset/table and a documented schema.
- Pricing preview supports selecting an existing price profile or entering a temporary slab for quick simulation.
- Component implemented as design system token with accessible keyboard interactions and mobile breakpoints.

Design artifacts & prototypes:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/Usage-Tally-Accordion-2025 (prototype flows + component variants)
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Usage+Tally+Accordion+PRD
- Interactive prototype (staged): https://console-staging.redwood.ai/prototypes/usage-tally (internal)

Export schema (CSV columns):
- timestamp, route_id, route_name, model_id, model_variant, prompt_id, prompt_name, user_id_masked, messages_count, tokens_input, tokens_output, token_unit_cost_usd, total_cost_usd, pricing_profile_id, pricing_preview_note

Trade-offs discussed:
- Live aggregation vs precomputed slices: we prototyped both. Live aggregation gives freshest numbers but increases query cost and may exceed SLOs for large queries. Decision: show near-real-time for day/7d views, and force precomputed job for >30d exports.
- Inline pricing simulator complexity: we limit to slab and tiered previews initially to avoid overwhelming the UI; negotiated/contracted pricing will be a follow-up.
- Attribution depth: variable depth (3 layers max) to keep the accordion compact; deep lineage links out to a dedicated 'Cost Lineage' page.

Engineering notes for handoff:
- Suggested data endpoints: /v1/console/usage/tally (collapsed), /v1/console/usage/tally/expanded (attribution + top contributors), /v1/console/usage/export (CSV/BigQuery).
- Instrumentation: include tracing id in export and permalink (trace_id, export_job_id).
- Performance SLO: expand action must render within 350ms for datasets <= 1000 routes; for larger selections, show skeleton + async job status.

Accessibility & localization:
- Ensure accordion toggles have aria-expanded, aria-controls, and keyboard focus states.
- Exports must include UTF-8 BOM and support localized number formatting on export (configurable).

Open questions:
- Should pricing previews default to the customer's committed rate if present? (PM leaning: yes, but engineering flagged data availability gaps).
- Do we allow non-admins to stream to BigQuery, or restrict to roles with dataset write permissions? (Security to weigh in).

Next steps:
- Finalize export schema with Data team (ENG-16824).
- Dev spike to validate /export API and BigQuery streaming permissions.
- Design review with PM and Eng on 2025-03-07.

Links to related tickets and artifacts:
- Mock GH PR for API contract: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4521
- Analytics event map: https://docs.redwood.ai/analytics/usage-tally-event-map.xlsx
comments: 2025-02-24 — Amira Patel: Initial concept draft uploaded to Figma; shared with PMs for early feedback. Noted that the collapsed row needs to preserve left alignment across responsive widths.
2025-02-28 — Jae Park (Eng): Reviewed trade-offs; recommends async precompute for >30d exports. Assigned ENG-16824 for API contract.
2025-03-02 — Laura Chen (PM): PM review: prioritize CSV for GA, BigQuery as opt-in. Suggest adding pricing preview presets (slab/flat).
2025-03-04 — Sofia Martinez (Design): Updated prototype to include pricing presets and inline help flyouts. Added keyboard-only interactions and aria labels.
2025-03-05 — Security (Sean Riley): Quick check: BigQuery stream should be gated by RBAC. Marking security_review_required=false for design, but request a short security sync before dev start.
